title: Gujarat Titans Crush CSK by 89 Runs in Chennai's Biggest IPL Defeat as Dhoni Era Fades to Black
excerpt: Sai Sudharsan's 84 and a three-wicket burst from Kagiso Rabada seal GT's playoff spot while CSK crash out at 12 points — and MS Dhoni's future remains an open wound
body:
There was no guard of honour, no farewell lap, no microphone handed to a legend for one last speech. When Chennai Super Kings were bowled out for 140 in just 13.4 overs at the Narendra Modi Stadium on Thursday — their biggest defeat by runs in IPL history — the 2026 season simply ended, and with it, perhaps, an era.

Gujarat Titans' 89-run annihilation of CSK was clinical in every dimension. Batting first, GT piled up 229/4 on the back of Sai Sudharsan's elegant 84 off 48 balls and Shubman Gill's assured 64. Jos Buttler provided the late acceleration with a quickfire cameo that carried the total beyond what CSK's depleted bowling could defend.

The opening stand between Gill and Sudharsan — worth 125 runs — was the tournament's third-highest this season. Sudharsan, who finished the league stage with 638 runs and the Orange Cap firmly in his grasp, played with the authority of a batsman in the form of his life: drives through cover, pulls dispatched with minimal fuss, and a six over long-on that announced the intent for the evening.

## CSK's collapse

Chennai's reply was a procession. Ruturaj Gaikwad fell for a golden duck in the first over — caught at slip off Mohammed Siraj attempting an ambitious drive — and the innings never recovered. Kagiso Rabada extracted sharp movement with the new ball, dismissing both Sanju Samson and Shivam Dube in a devastating three-over spell that read 3-0-18-3.

The middle order offered token resistance, but with the required rate climbing beyond 12 an over by the tenth, wickets tumbled in pursuit of impossible acceleration. CSK were 78/6 at the halfway mark and were bowled out with 38 balls unused.

Rashid Khan's death stare toward Dube after trapping him lbw became the match's most replayed moment — a veteran spinner revelling in the intensity of a high-stakes contest. Gill, captaining from the slips, took a spectacular one-handed catch to dismiss Dube, adding to the highlights reel.

## What it means for the table

The victory took Gujarat to 18 points and confirmed their spot in the top two. CSK finished on 12 points from 14 matches — their worst league-stage record since the 2020 UAE season, when they failed to qualify for the first time in franchise history.

For GT captain Shubman Gill, who crossed 6,000 career T20 runs during the innings and became the first player to score 600-plus runs in consecutive IPL seasons, the performance was a statement ahead of the playoffs. His side have won their last three matches and carry serious momentum into the knockout stage.

## The Dhoni question

The elephant in every CSK conversation remains MS Dhoni. Ruled out of the final league match against GT with a thumb injury, Dhoni watched from the hotel as his team's season unravelled. At 44, with a body that has borne the demands of professional sport for over two decades, the question of whether Chennai's most iconic captain has played his last IPL match hangs heavier than ever.

There has been no official retirement announcement. CSK's management has been characteristically tight-lipped. But the images from the franchise's social media — retrospective photo compilations, teammates posting heart emojis — suggest the inner circle knows something the public does not yet.

For the millions of NRI fans who grew up watching Dhoni's helicopter shots on grainy streams across US college dorms and UK living rooms, the possibility that it ended not with a final flourish but with a thumb injury in the Ahmedabad hotel room is a bitter pill. Cricket rarely offers the ending its heroes deserve.

CSK will regroup. They always do. But whether the yellow jersey will carry the number 7 when IPL 2027 begins next March is the question that will define this off-season.
